Definition: from G5046; to complete, i.e. (literally) accomplish, or (figuratively) consummate (in character):--consecrate, finish, fulfil, make) perfect.
BiblicalUsage: The word is to make perfect, to bring to completion. Jesus says, I have glorified Thee on the earth, I have finished the work which Thou gavest Me to do, and on the cross, knowing that all things were now accomplished, He says, I thirst, that the scripture might be fulfilled. The captain of our salvation was made perfect through sufferings; love is made perfect in us, so that we may have boldness in the day of judgment; and Paul says, Not as though I had already attained, either were already perfect, but I follow after.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe finishing is the Lord's work: He finished what the Father gave Him, and He finishes His people. My position is that perfection is not my achievement but His completion, and the love made perfect in us is His love, not ours.
